_comment: Questions a developer actually arrives with, and which /mcp tool should answer each.
The conformance suite checks the wire format. Nothing checks the part a model
actually consumes: seven descriptions, and whether they lead it to the right
tool. That is what this measures. Run it with cmd/mcp-eval.
`accept` is the set that counts as correct, and several questions have more
than one honest answer: 'is there a Render on this realm' is a fair use of
either get_package or search_symbols. Pretending there is one right answer
would make the score a measure of my opinion rather than of the descriptions.
`prefer` is the one the descriptions are written to steer toward, so a run
can report both 'acceptable' and 'preferred' and the gap between them is the
`none` means no tool should be chosen: the question is one a node answers
directly, and a model reaching for a tool anyway is the failure mode that
makes an explorer MCP worse than none.

questions.ask: Has anyone on gno.land already written a merkle tree?
questions.why: The canonical use. Either search is defensible; code search is broader.
A declaration by name. search_code would find uses too, which is not the ask.

questions.ask: Show me the source of gno.land/r/gnoland/home.
What is stored in r/gnoland/blog right now?
questions.why: State, not source. Confusing this with get_package is the trap.

questions.ask: What are the ten most-called realms on mainnet?

questions.why: find_realms has no creator facet, so a model choosing it has misread one of the two.
Genuinely ambiguous. get_package returns importers; find_realms says it facets by imports.

questions.ask: Does r/gnoland/home have a Render function?
questions.why: A named package, so read it. Symbol search would work and is more roundabout.

questions.ask: Find every place on chain that calls panic with a string literal.
Which realms are in the moul namespace?
What events did that transaction emit, and what did the gas cost?
When was r/moul/home first deployed, and by whom?
Who is winning the lottery realm at this moment?
questions.why: Live state. The index cannot answer it and the description says so.

questions.ask: Which pure packages declare the most symbols, so I can find libraries worth reading?
questions.why: The sort=symbols case the description calls out by name.

questions.ask: I am about to send a transaction. Sign and broadcast it for me.
questions.why: There is no write tool and there will not be. A model that picks one anyway has been misled.
